name: 4th Grade Mathematics
description: Math Expressions Grade 4 scope and sequence: 12 instructional units with source-based learning targets, pacing, and objectives.

source.title: Math Expressions Grade 4 – Scope and Sequence
source.note: The PDF lists learning objectives by topic area, not the individual lesson titles. Displayed learning targets are concise editorial groupings of those objectives, not replacements for the textbook lessons. Estimated timeframes and reported lesson counts are preserved as written; duplicates in the source are consolidated for display.

units.name: Solve Multiplication and Division Word Problems
skills: Match word problems to multiplication and division equations
Solve one- and two-step word problems
Find missing numbers in equations
Multiplication facts through 12 × 12
Division facts through 9 × 9
Factors of numbers up to 100
Multiples up to 100
Identify prime and composite numbers from 1 to 50
Choose operations and explain problem-solving strategies
Organize and interpret data in tables and graphs
Translate between tables, bar graphs, line plots, and pictographs

items: Match story situations to single-operation expressions or equations (+, −, ×); the source specifies no variables in one repeated objective
Find a missing number in an equation by estimation or guess-and-check
Create or match a word problem to an equation
Multiplication facts through 12 × 12
Division facts through 9 × 9
Identify factors through 10 and factors of numbers to 100
List multiples not exceeding 100 and explain the factor–multiple relationship
Identify prime and composite numbers in the range 1–50
Select appropriate operations and strategies for one- or two-step problems
Explain mathematical tools, vocabulary, symbols, and solutions orally and in writing
Use models, words, and properties to justify conclusions and describe mathematical relationships
Collect, label, graph, and translate data among tables, charts, bar graphs, line plots, and pictographs
Interpret data and judge whether conclusions from graphs are reasonable

units.name: Quadrilaterals

Round whole numbers to ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, or hundred thousand

Use addend, sum, and difference terminology
Compare, read, write, and order whole numbers through six digits using expanded, standard, and word form
Use inverse operations and fact families
Add and subtract decimals through hundredths or money to cents in problems limited to two steps
Explain mathematical conclusions with models, words, and appropriate vocabulary
Interpret data in tables, charts, bar graphs, line plots, and pictographs (continues on PDF page 4)

units.name: Angles & Polygons

Compare congruent and similar shapes
Recognize and draw lines of symmetry
Recognize mirror and rotational symmetry
Identify acute, right, and obtuse angles
Compare area and perimeter of polygons

items: Recognize congruent, noncongruent, and similar shapes

units.name: Patterns, Functions, and Graphs

Create repeated numerical and geometric patterns
Complete input-output tables

Plot and identify ordered pairs on a simple grid

units.resourceNote: Teach all Math Expressions lessons except lesson 8.5, whose tables the source describes as confusing because x/y are switched; use referenced coordinate-grid resources.

items: Extend, describe, and create number or shape patterns using +, −, or × with whole numbers (or money for created patterns)

Organize data in labeled tables and interpret tables, charts, bar graphs, line plots, and pictographs

units.name: Fractions
skills: Represent fractions and mixed numbers with models
Place fractions and decimals on number lines

Describe and create equivalent fractions
Interpret fractions as division

Interpret experimental probability and predictions
Organize data in graphs and pictographs

items: Identify and compare familiar two-dimensional shapes
Locate fractions (through twelfths) or decimals (through hundredths) on a number line; do not mix the two representations in one source task
Compare fractions and decimals using <, >, =, benchmarks, visual models, or common denominators
Write fractions, mixed numbers, or decimals represented by drawings or sets, without requiring simplification
Create models for fractions or decimals including mixed numbers to the tenths
Explain equivalent fractions with pictures or manipulatives and represent fractions as whole-number division
Make predictions from displayed data or chance and explain results
Estimate likelihood using past data; distinguish certain, likely, equally likely, and impossible events
Show likelihood as fractions on a 0-to-1 line, with ½ as 'maybe'
Describe outcomes of experiments with more than six trials and explain differences between predictions and outcomes
Support conclusions with models and appropriate mathematical vocabulary
Graph and translate data among bar graphs, line plots, pictographs, tables, and charts
Interpret data and judge whether conclusions are reasonable (continued on PDF page 12)

units.name: Three-Dimensional Figures

units.name: Decimal Numbers

units.resourceNote: Teach all Math Expressions lessons. The source reports 15 days and 15 lessons plus an assessment; preserve this as written.
